symptom: The UC-13 database container could not publish host port 3306, so the fresh backend and frontend runtime could not start.
evidence: Read-only port inspection identified a researcher-controlled host mysqld process listening on TCP port 3306; no credentials, database payloads, or raw logs were retained.

root_cause.summary: An external host MySQL process already owns port 3306.

actions: Queried the incident index before collecting bounded evidence.
Inspected Compose state and resolved the host listener owner without stopping or modifying the external process.
Stopped at the mandatory UC-13 RQ3 repair-authorization gate without changing Compose configuration.
After researcher authorization, used a temporary non-repository Compose override to publish MySQL on host port 3307 while preserving internal service port 3306.
resolution: A temporary non-repository Compose override mapped 127.0.0.1:3307 to the database service's internal port 3306; the database reached healthy without disturbing the external host mysqld process.
reusable_resolution: With researcher authorization, use a non-conflicting host-port mapping or remove the unnecessary database host publication while preserving internal Compose service port 3306.
prevention: Check host port 3306 ownership before starting Compose and avoid terminating unrelated host database services.
